subject: Lab window booking & routing ops — confirm test profile and slots
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme.ai>, eng-lab@acme.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Lab window booking & routing ops — confirm test profile and slots

Hi Alice / Eng lab team,

Thanks for agreeing to a hands-on session to validate throughput/routing for the storefront recommendation pipeline. To get us scheduled and minimize churn on day-of, proposing the following 2-hour lab windows (all PST):

- Option A: Tue 2026-11-30 09:00–11:00
- Option B: Tue 2026-11-30 13:00–15:00
- Option C: Wed 2026-12-01 10:00–12:00

High level objectives for the session:
- Prompt & prompt-routing review (verify golden path and fallback routing)
- Warm-up & smoke test with representative prompts
- Incremental load run to throughput target of ~500 req/s sustained for 10 min
- 5-minute peak burst test to validate autoscaling and p95 latency SLO (target p95 < 200 ms)
- Collect token-level cost and latency breakdowns for your engineering team

What we need from you before we lock a slot:
1) Confirm which window works (A/B/C)
2) Provide a small sample workload CSV or link (request distribution, avg tokens)
3) Let us know if your network team needs IPs whitelisted (we will provide ranges)
4) Confirm the model variant you want us to run (e.g., open-7B-quant or rdx-3b-fp16)

Attached: throughput-test-plan.pdf (high-level run steps + measurement checklist).

If we get a slot confirmed today we'll send a calendar invite + brief runbook.

Thanks!
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-lab@acme.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Lab window booking & routing ops — confirm test profile and slots

Hi Dylan,

Thanks — Option B (Tue 11/30 13:00–15:00 PST) works best for our infra team.

A few quick notes from our side:
- I've uploaded a small sample workload to the shared bucket: https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/datasets/rdx_poc_profile_v1.csv
  - avg tokens/request ~ 180, 70% read-only scoring, 30% multi-turn edit flow
- We'll need the Redwood test harness IPs to be whitelisted against our VIP (please send ranges)
- Do you provide the load harness container image or do we run clients from our infra? Either is fine; we prefer your harness to ensure consistent measurement.

Once I have the harness URL and IP ranges I'll loop in our network security owner to get the allowlist prepped.

Cheers,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Engineering Programs | Acme Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Lab window booking & routing ops — confirm test profile and slots

On Mon, Nov 29, 2026 at 9:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> ...Attached: throughput-test-plan.pdf (high-level run steps + measurement checklist).

Thanks for the quick reply, Alice — we'll provide the harness and a pre-built container image (rwi-loadgen:stable) you can run or we can run it from Redwood-managed hosts. A few operational details: 

- Test harness: rwi-loadgen v2 (we'll post the run instructions + docker image tag)
- IP ranges to whitelist: 34.120.16.0/20 and 34.108.0.0/20 (Redwood-managed load agents)
- Baseline SLO suggestion: p95 < 250 ms for initial ramp; we can tighten to 200 ms after the first full run once we have telemetry.
- Can we get the prompt sets you want exercised? Put them in the Drive folder (I've added a PromptSet/ directory).

Plan for Tue 13:00–15:00 (Option B):
- 13:00–13:15: Setup, whitelisting smoke test, confirm model variant
- 13:15–13:35: Prompt review and routing configuration validation (golden path + fallback)
- 13:35–13:50: Warm-up run (10–20 req/s) and verify correctness
- 13:50–14:30: Stepped load to 500 req/s sustained for 10 min (collect p50/p95/p99)
- 14:30–14:45: Burst test and failover exercise for routing fallback
- 14:45–15:00: Wrap, quick debrief, next steps

I've attached runbook-v1.md with the exact command flags and telemetry endpoints. Please confirm you can host the prompt CSV at the S3 path Alice shared, or paste it into the Drive folder.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick operational add-on:

- Routing policy: we'll propose a two-tier policy for the session — golden_path -> rdx-7b; fallback -> open-3b-quant. During the stepped load we'll enable a 10% canary to route a subset of traffic to fallback and compare latency/cost.
- Telemetry: remind the team to enable token-level cost metrics in the console for the run (Marissa has set a 30-day retention on the PoC org so we can pull charts next week).
- Can someone from Acme confirm who will accept the calendar invite? If it's a group alias I'll add it directly so invites don't bounce.

I added a short prompt checklist to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcExAMPLEprompt-sets

Marissa

- 13:35–13:50: Warm-up run
- 13:50–14:30: Stepped load to 500 req/s (10 min steady-state)

Artifacts we'll share during the session:
